title: Add wasm-backed RAG devcontainer and Rust tool adapter
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds a compact devcontainer-based RAG quickstart that demonstrates a Rust tool adapter compiled to WebAssembly for local tool-calling development. No API changes.
description: Motivation: provide a low-friction local authoring experience for RAG/agent examples that lets engineers iterate on tool-calling logic without heavy native dependencies. This PR adds a devcontainer + lightweight wasm runtime workflow and a Rust-based adapter that compiles to WASM and exposes a small JSON-RPC tool interface used in our sample agent. The goal is to show how teams can prototype deterministic tool bindings (retrieval, vector store access, simple FAAS) using a Rust adapter that runs in the browser/Node via WASM or locally in the devcontainer. Summary of changes: initial scaffold for devcontainer and dotfiles, CI matrix updates for building WASM artifacts, a new examples/rust-wasm-tool-adapter directory with a mini Rust crate (tokio-free, serde-enabled) and build script for wasm-pack/wasm32-unknown-unknown target, a TypeScript shim that loads the WASM module and exposes a tool-calling shim used by the RAG example, updated quickstart README with step-by-step local run instructions, and small test harness with an emulated retrieval backend for deterministic tests. Why this is different: existing quickstarts focus on Node/Python runtime adapters or server-side binaries. This introduces a compact, cross-platform path (WASM) that removes the need for platform-specific toolchains for contributors and demonstrates how to keep tool logic close to the UI for prototyping. Backwards compatibility: all changes are non-breaking examples/docs only. Implementation notes: the Rust adapter exposes a single async entrypoint process_call(request_json) -> response_json, implemented as synchronous bridging in the WASM build to keep the example minimal. The devcontainer includes cargo + wasm-pack, Node 20, pnpm, and a small script (scripts/build-wasm.sh) that builds the adapter and packs the TS shim. The README contains a short troubleshooting section for common devcontainer permissions and Docker resource tips. Testing: added a node-based integration test that runs the wasm adapter in a headless Node+wasm environment and validates expected tool outputs for fixed prompts. CI: matrix now includes linux-node-wasm and devcontainer build smoke test. Related: ENG-4123 for local dev experience improvements, PM-88 for quickstart analytics tracking.

merge_summary: Merged by squash on 2026-02-20 by Evan Brooks. Merge commit summary: 'examples: add wasm-backed RAG devcontainer and Rust tool adapter (Maya Chen)'. Release tagging: none — docs/examples only.
notes_for_reviewers: Focus review on README clarity, CI reliability for wasm builds, and the minimal security guidance in the Security Considerations section. The wasm adapter is intentionally small and synchronous-ish to minimize cognitive load for readers. If we want to expand, follow-up PRs should add additional examples (vector store access, secure key handling) behind feature flags.
user_impact: Developers: easier cross-platform local prototyping for RAG tool-calling. No runtime or API changes for Redwood customers. Docs-only change for public quickstarts.
changelog_entry: examples: add wasm-backed devcontainer and rust tool adapter (quickstart)
audits: manual security review suggested before converting example to production reference; CI includes basic wasm size and compatibility checks.
testing_instructions:
1) Open repository in devcontainer
2) ./examples/rust-wasm-tool-adapter/build.sh
3) pnpm install && pnpm run test:wasm
4) Start the example application: pnpm start and hit http://localhost:3000/quickstart-wasm to exercise the tool-calling flow
Expect deterministic responses from the emulated retrieval backend for the sample prompts.
discussion_threads: Two threads: 1) CI infra tweaks for wasm target (resolved), 2) Security considerations for local WASM execution (documented, follow-up work recommended).
